title.narrative: Solomon Islands Sustainable Mining Development Technical Assistance Project

description.narrative: The development objective of the Sustainable Mining Development Technical Assistance Project for Solomon Islands is to strengthen the capacity of regulatory institutions to implement revised mining and related laws consistently, transparently and effectively. The project comprises of three components. The first component, completion of the regulatory framework will support Ministry of Mines, Energy and Rural Electrification (MMERE) to complete the design of the regulatory framework in line with the national minerals policy (NMP). It consists of following sub-components: (i) policy, plans, and legislation; and (ii) institutional structures and functions. The second component, strengthening the capacity of regulatory institutions will support building capacity of government regulatory institutions to fulfill their functions consistently, transparently, and effectively and support MMERE to overcome near term operational challenges. It consists of following sub-components: (i) mineral rights management; (ii) mineral revenue management; (iii) geo-data management; (iv) operational support; and (v) independent advisory institution. The third component, project management will fund: (a) the operational and technical assistance needed by MMERE as the implementing agency to manage the project during implementation for which a project management unit (PMU) will be established to exercise project management responsibilities on MMERE's behalf; and (b) selected equipment costs and office refurbishment at MMERE.
To strengthen the capacity of regulatory institutions to implement revised mining and related laws consistently, transparently and effectively.

condition.narrative: 1. The Recipient shall vest responsibility for carrying out the day-to-day coordination, management and implementation of theProject to its MMERE, with the MMERE Permanent Secretary serving as the Project Director. Schedule 2, Section I.A.1.

2. No later than one (1) month from the Effective Date (or such later date as may be agreed in writing between the Recipient andthe Association), the Recipient shall establish and thereafter maintain throughout the period of Project implementation the ProjectSteering Committee (“PSC”), with composition, resources, and terms of reference acceptable to the Association. Schedule 2, SectionI.A.2.

3. No later than one (1) month from the Effective Date (or such later date as may be agreed in writing between the Recipient andthe Association), the Recipient shall establish and thereafter maintain throughout the period of Project implementation theTechnical Working Group (“TWG”), with composition, resources, and terms of reference acceptable to the Association, to provideoperational oversight of the Project at a technical level. Schedule 2, Section I.A.3.

4. No later than three (3) months from the Effective Date (or such later date as may be agreed in writing between the Recipient andthe Association), the Recipient shall establish within the MMERE and thereafter maintain throughout the period of Projectimplementation the Project Management Unit (“PMU”), with composition, resources, and terms of reference acceptable to theAssociation. Schedule 2, Section I.A.4.

5. No later than two (2) months after the Effective Date (or such later date as may be agreed in writing between the Recipient andthe Association), the Recipient through the MMERE shall prepare and adopt a Project Operations Manual, satisfactory to theAssociation. Schedule 2, Section I.B.1.

6. The Recipient through the MMERE's PMU shall prepare and furnish to the Association, no later than two (2) months after theEffective Date and February 1 of each subsequent year during the implementation of the Project (or such later interval or date asthe Association may agree) following approval by the PSC, for the Association's review and no-objection, an Annual Work Plan andBudget. Schedule 2, Section I.C.1.

7.i The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance with the Environmental and Social Standards, in amanner acceptable to the Association. Schedule 2, Section I.D.1.7.ii Without limitation upon paragraph 1 above, the Recipientshall ensure that the Project is implemented in accordance with the Environmental and Social Commitment Plan, in a manneracceptable to the Association. Schedule 2, Section I.D.2. The Recipient shall ensure that: (a) all consultancies related totechnical assistance, design and capacity building under the Project, the application of whose results could have environmental,social and health and safety implications, shall only be undertaken pursuant to terms of reference reviewed and found satisfactoryby the Association; and (b) such terms of reference shall require the technical assistance, design and capacity building activitiesto take into account the requirements of the applicable ESSs. Schedule 2, Section I.D.7.

8. The Recipient shall ensure that all technical assistance under the Project shall be: (a) consistent with the principles andstandards in the NMP and international best practice; and (b) satisfactory to the Association. Schedule 2, Section IV.A.

title.narrative: Participation rate of women in committees and boards established by communities to negotiate access, community development and other agreements provided for in the mining legislation (Cumulative)

comment.narrative: The current participation rate is at 19% which falls short of the 30% target for year 4 but improved from the 17% previously reached. This shows positive results from MMERE. This is making progress but yearly targets should be revised for practicality. MMERE has recently created a Community Liaison Section within the Mines Division, a significant milestone achieved under SISMDTAP for community engagement. The Ministry of Public Service has approved four positions for this section, currently in the interviewing stage. This new unit will serve as an intermediary to address issues and facilitate communication between MMERE, the community, mining companies, and other affected parties regarding socio-economic development in the mining sector. This unit will also be advocating for mining-affected communities to promote active stakeholder participation in mining governance by working to improve women's participation rate.

title.narrative: Proportion of licensed mining operations for which a recent inspection report has been uploaded to a MMERE inspection database (Cumulative)

comment.narrative: The project exceeded its target of 75% in year 3, achieving a remarkable 88% compliance rate for mine inspections. This data was verified by viewing the inspection reports for each active ML stored in the inspectorate section. currently, performance for this particular indicator has declined slightly, with only 35% achieved against 90% target. The primary reason for this shortfall is budget constraints, which have limited the inspectorate team's ability to mobilize to mining sites.

title.narrative: Women's employment in mining sector increased (Cumulative)

comment.narrative:
While the year 4 target was 25%, the project achieved only 11%, up from the previous year's 9%. This data includes both public and private employment. Some mining operations, like Pacific Nickel Mining Kolosori, have had to scale down or stop operations, affecting employment.
To achieve this indicator, MMERE is committed to increasing women's employment in the mining sector through its GESI Strategy. This strategy aims to ensure inclusive, equitable, and beneficial mining sector development in the Solomon Islands. The Draft GESI Strategy, section 6, Strategy 3, outlines actions to expand employment and economic opportunities for women, including promoting recruitment, retention, and career advancement through targeted programs, training, and mentorship.

title.narrative: Reduced time between lodging applications and approval hearings

comment.narrative: The Ministry of Mines, Energy and Rural Electrification (MMERE) has significantly reduced the average processing time for new exploration license applications, achieving a one-month processing time, exceeding the target of two months set for Year 3. This accomplishment demonstrates MMERE's commitment to improving the efficiency and effectiveness of its services. The reduction in processing time reflects MMERE's dedication to providing a more efficient and responsive service to applicants and stakeholders. This achievement is attributed to the successful implementation of the Mining Cadaster Administration System (MCAS), a digital geo-referenced platform developed under the project.

title.narrative: Extent of forest loss in mining areas

comment.narrative: The dataset covers six sites across three provinces, namely Isabel, Choiseul and Guadalcanal. The overall average forest cover on the six sites is approximately 77.88%, with a total forest cover of 2,030 ha over 2,606 ha. This indicates that the extent which forest loss in mining areas is approximately 22.12% including water bodies.

title.narrative: An increase in the average ratio of actual royalty collection to collections at the nominal royalty rate (reduced leakage)

comment.narrative: To date, 156 shipments have been exported since the operation of active Mining License ( ML) holders in the country of which 14 are Nickle shipments and 142 are Gold& Silver shipments. The Royalty payment (3% of Gross product) has three different categories namely SIG (50% of Royalty), PG (10% of Royalty), and LO (40% of Royalty). The total Royalty collected on Average is 52.60.

title.narrative: An increase in the average ratio of actual royalty collection to collections at the nominal royalty rate (reduced leakage)

comment.narrative: Royalty collection has improved since MMERE has taken action for active mining companies in the Solomon Islands to comply and pay up their dues. GRML has so far paid SBD$14,892,226.38 of unpaid royalties (worth SBD$33M) to SIG. Through observation, it has been witnessed that the MMERE has stepped up and toughened up in ensuring all mining companies comply. To date, the actual royalty collection ratio stands at 91%: 9%, showing improvement from the baseline of 50%:50%, reflecting improvement done to reduce leakage and better collection performance. This also shows that year 4 target (80%) has been overachieved.

title.narrative: Increased monitoring of contractual and regulatory arrangements and their enforcement to ensure alignment with National Minerals Policy and applicable international standards

comment.narrative: The Mineral Resources Bill 2025 is currently with the Bills and Legislation Committee (BLC) deliberation phase, with enactment delayed by stakeholder concerns and pending provincial hearings. Regulations cannot proceed without the bill's passage, projected for Q4 2025. This PDO is at risk of meeting the target, as it hinges on the legislative timeline. The Project and MMERE are heavily reliant on external processes (Parliament), which poses risks to meeting the target; however, MMERE is still optimistic that the Mineral Resources Bill passage will be enacted in Q4 2025, as it is a government priority.

title.narrative: Comprehensive public disclosure of cadastral records of license applications and awards and subsequent license management

comment.narrative: The indicator has been successfully met. The Mining Cadastre Administration System (MCAS) is the main system that was developed for government civil servants which is the MMERE, Mines Division. This system, MCAS comes with a portal, accessible to the public. The online portal is a completely separate application that connects to MCAS. This online portal is also linked with the MMERE website (www.mmere.gov.sb) . Currently, MCAS is used by Mines Division for their purpose and the public with the mining companies are using the online portal to make new applications, reporting obligations, and even due diligence checks on applications in preparation for Mines and Minerals Board meetings. This demonstrates improvement in transparency and efficiency in the processing of applications and permits within MMERE and public disclosure of cadastral records.

The implementation of MCAS a significant achievement for the MMERE and is now an integral part of Ministry's daily operations and has been recognized for its effectiveness and the transparency it brings to managing cadastral records.

Mining Bill based on the NMP enacted

comment.narrative: The enactment of the Mining Bill, a key project milestone, has not yet been achieved. MMERE has completed 70% of the mineral Resources Bill (MRB), with the remaining 30% currently in the government's hands. The next steps include the MRB going before the Bills Legislation Committee, having its First, Second, and Third Readings in Parliament, receiving Royal Assent, and being gazetted to become effective, all tentatively scheduled for the last quarter of 2025.Government and MMERE to fast-track the process, as with the current trend, this could be enacted in early 2026.
